es: Analizar un artículo de opinión: localizar la postura, los apoyos, una concesión, el lenguaje cauteloso y las estructuras clave.

teaching.en: In my view, schools give too much homework.
teaching.es: En mi opinión, los colegios ponen demasiados deberes.
teaching.explanationEs: In my view presenta la postura del autor: es la idea que defiende todo el texto.
segments: In my view, schools
give too much homework.
teaching.audioText: In my view, schools give too much homework.

teaching.en: There is evidence that tired students make more mistakes.
teaching.es: Hay pruebas de que los estudiantes cansados cometen más errores.
teaching.explanationEs: Evidence introduce un apoyo: un dato o una prueba que sostiene la postura.
segments: There is evidence that tired
students make more mistakes.
teaching.audioText: There is evidence that tired students make more mistakes.

teaching.en: Admittedly, some homework helps students remember things.
teaching.es: Es cierto que algunos deberes ayudan a los estudiantes a recordar cosas.
teaching.explanationEs: Admittedly es la concesión: reconoce un punto del otro lado sin cambiar de postura.
segments: Admittedly, some homework helps
students remember things.
teaching.audioText: Admittedly, some homework helps students remember things.

teaching.en: However, if schools had asked students earlier, homework would not be such a problem today.
teaching.es: Sin embargo, si los colegios hubieran preguntado antes a los estudiantes, los deberes no serían tanto problema hoy.
teaching.explanationEs: However vuelve a la postura; además aparece un condicional mixto.
segments: However, if schools had asked students earlier, homework
would not be such a problem today.
teaching.audioText: However, if schools had asked students earlier, homework would not be such a problem today.

teaching.en: Many teachers claim that homework improves grades, but this is arguably not always true.
teaching.es: Muchos profesores afirman que los deberes mejoran las notas, pero podría decirse que no siempre es cierto.
teaching.explanationEs: Claim reporta una afirmación ajena; arguably suaviza la opinión del autor.
segments: Many teachers claim that homework improves grades,
but this is arguably not always true.
teaching.audioText: Many teachers claim that homework improves grades, but this is arguably not always true.

prompt.es: En este texto, ¿cuál es la postura del autor?

choices.text: Children spend too much time on screens.
Screens help children learn.
Children sleep more with screens.

feedback.es: La postura es la idea que el autor defiende: aparece tras In my view. Las otras dos son una concesión y una idea que contradice el texto.

hint.es: La postura suele aparecer después de In my view.

origin.text: In my view, children spend too much time on screens. Studies show that they sleep less. Admittedly, screens can help them learn. However, the balance is wrong.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase es el apoyo del autor?

choices.text: Many teachers claim that homework improves grades.
There is evidence that it often only makes students tired.
Many teachers give too little homework.

feedback.es: El apoyo aporta pruebas: There is evidence that… sostiene la postura. Otra frase atribuye una afirmación a otras personas y la tercera no aparece en el texto.

hint.es: El apoyo aporta pruebas: busca evidence.

origin.text: Many teachers claim that homework improves grades. However, there is evidence that it often only makes students tired.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es cierto que algunos deberes ayudan, pero deberían ser más cortos.»

feedback.es: Admittedly concede un punto al otro lado antes de volver a la postura con but o however.

hint.es: Es la palabra que concede un punto al otro lado.

origin.text: ___, some homework helps, but it should be shorter.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con su función en un artículo de opinión.

feedback.es: Cada expresión cumple un papel: presenta la postura, aporta pruebas, concede un punto o suaviza la afirmación.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la concesión del autor?

choices.text: Cleaner air would help everyone.
City centres should be closed to cars.
Shops might lose some customers.

feedback.es: La concesión reconoce un punto del otro lado: las tiendas podrían perder clientes. Las otras dos frases son un apoyo y la postura.

origin.text: Some people say that city centres should be closed to cars. Admittedly, shops might lose some customers. However, cleaner air would help everyone.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Sin embargo, el resultado sería distinto si nos hubieran preguntado.»

answer.text: However the result would be different if they had asked us

feedback.es: Es un condicional mixto: if + had + participio para la causa pasada y would be para el resultado de hoy.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase marca la postura final del autor?

choices.text: Cities should build more bike lanes.
Bikes are dangerous in cities.
There have been accidents.

feedback.es: La postura final aparece tras In my view: las ciudades deberían construir más carriles bici. Las otras frases son la opinión ajena y una concesión.

origin.text: Some people believe that bikes are dangerous in cities. Admittedly, there have been accidents. However, riders who wear helmets are rarely hurt. In my view, cities should build more bike lanes.

prompt.es: Completa: «El plan es barato. Sin embargo, no es muy práctico.»

feedback.es: However abre una frase que contrasta con la anterior y va seguido de coma.

origin.text: The plan is cheap. ___, it is not very practical.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase afirma algo con cautela, sin asegurarlo del todo?

choices.text: This is definitely the best solution.
This is arguably the best solution.
This is the best solution, and nobody can disagree.

feedback.es: Arguably suaviza la afirmación. Las otras dos la presentan como una verdad absoluta.

origin.text: Quieres decir que algo es probablemente la mejor solución, pero sin afirmarlo del todo.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con la estructura del nivel que contiene.

pairs: The writer admitted that she had been wrong.
She had her text checked by a friend.
She had been writing for hours.
If she had waited, she would be calmer now.

feedback.es: Cada frase usa una estructura distinta: reporte, causativo, pasado perfecto continuo y condicional mixto.

pairs: The writer admitted that she had been wrong.
She had her text checked by a friend.

If she had waited, she would be calmer now.

prompt.es: ¿Qué dato del texto apoya la postura del autor?

choices.text: It costs more.
Public libraries should stay open until ten.

answer.text: In my view we should read more slowly

feedback.es: In my view presenta la postura del autor, seguida de la idea que defiende.

es: Mejorar un borrador corrigiendo formas y mejorando conectores, precisión y repeticiones, y registrar cada cambio.

teaching.en: Mia revised her draft carefully before she sent it.
teaching.es: Mia revisó su borrador con cuidado antes de enviarlo.
teaching.explanationEs: Revise = mirar de nuevo y mejorar; el borrador (draft) todavía no es la versión final.
segments: Mia revised her draft carefully
before she sent it.
teaching.audioText: Mia revised her draft carefully before she sent it.

teaching.en: She replaced the vague word thing with the exact word ticket.
teaching.es: Sustituyó la palabra vaga thing por la palabra exacta ticket.
teaching.explanationEs: Una palabra vaga (thing, stuff) se reemplaza por otra precisa.
segments: She replaced the vague word thing
with the exact word ticket.
teaching.audioText: She replaced the vague word thing with the exact word ticket.

teaching.en: The second paragraph was wordy, so she cut it to two clear sentences.
teaching.es: El segundo párrafo tenía demasiadas palabras, así que lo redujo a dos frases claras.
teaching.explanationEs: Un texto wordy dice poco con muchas palabras; se mejora cortando.
segments: The second paragraph was wordy, so she
cut it to two clear sentences.
teaching.audioText: The second paragraph was wordy, so she cut it to two clear sentences.

teaching.en: After checking the tenses, she wrote: I have lived here since June.
teaching.es: Después de comprobar los tiempos verbales, escribió: Vivo aquí desde junio.
teaching.explanationEs: Revisar los tiempos: since + punto de inicio pide present perfect.
segments: After checking the tenses, she wrote:
I have lived here since June.
teaching.audioText: After checking the tenses, she wrote: I have lived here since June.

teaching.en: Finally, she read the text aloud and cut a repeated sentence.
teaching.es: Por último, leyó el texto en voz alta y eliminó una frase repetida.
teaching.explanationEs: Leer en voz alta ayuda a oír repeticiones y frases torpes.
segments: Finally, she read the text aloud
and cut a repeated sentence.
teaching.audioText: Finally, she read the text aloud and cut a repeated sentence.

prompt.es: ¿Qué revisión sustituye la palabra vaga por una precisa?

choices.text: I bought some stuff for school. It was cheap.
I bought a backpack for school. It was cheap.
I bought a thing for school. It was cheap.

feedback.es: La revisión cambia thing por backpack, una palabra exacta. La segunda versión cambia a otra palabra vaga y la tercera no cambia nada.

hint.es: Busca la versión que nombra exactamente el objeto.

origin.text: Borrador: «I bought a thing for school. It was cheap.» (La cosa es una mochila.)

prompt.es: Completa: «Leí el texto en voz alta antes de enviarlo.»

feedback.es: Aloud significa en voz alta: leer así ayuda a oír errores y repeticiones.

hint.es: Es el adverbio que significa «en voz alta».

origin.text: I read the text ___ before I sent it.

prompt.es: ¿Qué revisión muestra bien la relación entre las dos ideas?

choices.text: The trip was expensive. Therefore, we enjoyed it very much.
The trip was expensive. For example, we enjoyed it very much.
The trip was expensive. However, we enjoyed it very much.

feedback.es: Las dos ideas se oponen (era caro, pero gustó), así que hace falta un conector de contraste: however.

hint.es: Las dos ideas se oponen: busca el conector de contraste.

origin.text: Borrador: «The trip was expensive. We enjoyed it very much.»

prompt.es: ¿Qué corrección arregla el tiempo verbal del borrador?

choices.text: I lived in Lima last year.
I have been living in Lima last year.
I am living in Lima last year.

feedback.es: Last year es una fecha terminada, así que se usa pasado simple: lived. Present perfect o continuo no combinan con un momento cerrado.

origin.text: Borrador: «I have lived in Lima last year.»

prompt.es: Completa: «Revisé mi borrador dos veces» y «El párrafo tenía demasiadas palabras».

feedback.es: Un draft es la versión previa al texto final, y un párrafo con demasiadas palabras es wordy.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la mejor versión del borrador, sin repeticiones?

choices.text: My brother is tall. He is very tall. He plays football and he is very good.
My brother is very tall, so he plays football, and he is very good at it.
My brother is tall, although he plays football, and he is very good.

feedback.es: Une las ideas con conectores y elimina la repetición de very tall y very good. Las otras versiones repiten o usan un conector que no encaja.

choices.text: I wish I studied more.
I wish I will study more.

es: Combinar la información de un texto y de un audio sobre el mismo tema: detectar acuerdos, diferencias y una conclusión con evidencia.

teaching.en: Both the article and the radio report say that prices have risen.
teaching.es: Tanto el artículo como el informe de radio dicen que los precios han subido.
teaching.explanationEs: Both une dos fuentes que coinciden en un dato.
segments: Both the article and the radio
report say that prices have risen.
teaching.audioText: Both the article and the radio report say that prices have risen.

teaching.en: The article says the park will close in June, whereas the radio report says it will stay open.
teaching.es: El artículo dice que el parque cerrará en junio, mientras que el informe de radio dice que seguirá abierto.
teaching.explanationEs: Whereas contrasta dos datos que no coinciden.
segments: The article says the park will close in June,
whereas the radio report says it will stay open.
teaching.audioText: The article says the park will close in June, whereas the radio report says it will stay open.

teaching.en: Unlike the article, the speaker thinks the new rule is unfair.
teaching.es: A diferencia del artículo, el hablante piensa que la nueva norma es injusta.
teaching.explanationEs: Unlike + fuente marca que la otra fuente piensa distinto.
segments: Unlike the article, the speaker thinks
the new rule is unfair.
teaching.audioText: Unlike the article, the speaker thinks the new rule is unfair.

teaching.en: Similarly, both sources mention the cost, but they disagree about who will pay.
teaching.es: Del mismo modo, las dos fuentes mencionan el costo, pero no están de acuerdo en quién pagará.
teaching.explanationEs: Similarly añade un punto en común; but introduce la diferencia.
segments: Similarly, both sources mention the cost, but
they disagree about who will pay.
teaching.audioText: Similarly, both sources mention the cost, but they disagree about who will pay.

teaching.en: The sources differ on the date, but the conclusion is clear: the event will happen in summer.
teaching.es: Las fuentes difieren en la fecha, pero la conclusión es clara: el evento será en verano.
teaching.explanationEs: Differ on + dato señala en qué no coinciden; la conclusión resume lo que se puede afirmar.
segments: The sources differ on the date, but the conclusion
is clear: the event will happen in summer.
teaching.audioText: The sources differ on the date, but the conclusion is clear: the event will happen in summer.

es: Presentar y defender una postura oral de un minuto con introducción, dos argumentos, una hipótesis, una concesión y un cierre.

teaching.en: My topic today is whether schools should start later.
teaching.es: Mi tema de hoy es si los colegios deberían empezar más tarde.
teaching.explanationEs: Una buena introducción dice el tema en una frase: My topic today is…
segments: My topic today is whether
schools should start later.
teaching.audioText: My topic today is whether schools should start later.

teaching.en: Firstly, teenagers need more sleep, and studies show that tired students learn less.
teaching.es: En primer lugar, los adolescentes necesitan dormir más, y los estudios muestran que los estudiantes cansados aprenden menos.
teaching.explanationEs: El primer argumento lleva firstly y una prueba que lo sostiene.
segments: Firstly, teenagers need more sleep, and studies
show that tired students learn less.
teaching.audioText: Firstly, teenagers need more sleep, and studies show that tired students learn less.

teaching.en: Secondly, a later start would reduce the stress of the morning rush.
teaching.es: En segundo lugar, empezar más tarde reduciría el estrés de las prisas de la mañana.
teaching.explanationEs: Secondly abre el segundo argumento; would + verbo base habla de un efecto posible.
segments: Secondly, a later start would reduce
the stress of the morning rush.
teaching.audioText: Secondly, a later start would reduce the stress of the morning rush.

teaching.en: Suppose schools started at nine; I think students would be calmer.
teaching.es: Supongamos que los colegios empezaran a las nueve; creo que los estudiantes estarían más tranquilos.
teaching.explanationEs: La hipótesis usa suppose + pasado simple y would + verbo base.
segments: Suppose schools started at nine; I
think students would be calmer.
teaching.audioText: Suppose schools started at nine; I think students would be calmer.

teaching.en: Admittedly, some parents would have to change their schedules.
teaching.es: Es cierto que algunos padres tendrían que cambiar sus horarios.
teaching.explanationEs: La concesión reconoce un punto contrario, sin abandonar la postura.
segments: Admittedly, some parents would have
to change their schedules.
teaching.audioText: Admittedly, some parents would have to change their schedules.

teaching.en: In short, a later start is a small change with a big benefit.
teaching.es: En resumen, empezar más tarde es un cambio pequeño con un gran beneficio.
teaching.explanationEs: El cierre repite tu postura en una frase corta: In short, …
segments: In short, a later start is a
small change with a big benefit.
teaching.audioText: In short, a later start is a small change with a big benefit.

answer.text: The youth club used to open on Saturdays, but since January it has been opening only on weekdays. The director told us that the club had run out of money, and Mr Lee said that many teenagers had nowhere else to go. If the club had asked for help earlier, it would still be open on Saturdays now, and I wish it had done that. In my view, this is arguably a mistake, because Saturday is the day when young people have the most free time. Admittedly, the club needs money. However, I think neighbours could help, and a small budget would give teenagers a safe place again. My plan is to ask the neighbours for help by March, and I am sure many of them would say yes. Final revision: I changed soon to by March, so the deadline is clear.
